selected_because: Thick acetate full-rim rectangle — the baseline case: large flat surfaces, visible bevel, chunky temples.

source.supplier_type: WooCommerce B2B catalog, ingested by apps/scraper
source.image_policy: Every photo the supplier publishes for this model is downloaded — one per colourway. The extra URLs on a product page (-300x123, -1024x419, …) are WordPress thumbnail resizes of the same shot and are skipped.
source.rights_note: Supplier product photography. Internal prototyping only — not cleared for redistribution.

measurements_mm.note: The supplier publishes a range per model because one model number covers several sizes. The photographed unit is one size inside that range and its exact size is not stated. Use `nominal` as the modelling target and the range as tolerance.

lens_height_b.note: Published as a coarse bucket (e.g. 41-50 mm), so it is a weak constraint.

derived_total_front_width.note: Excludes end-piece overhang; real total width typically runs 2-6 mm larger.

observed_construction.rim: full rim, thick glossy acetate, visible inner bevel groove
observed_construction.nose_pads: separate clear plastic pads on short metal arms
observed_construction.hardware: two silver rivets on each end piece, metal barrel hinge
observed_construction.markings: 'DC384 Capri' printed inside left temple, 'Frame China' inside right

geometry_hints_3d.basis: Typical values for this construction (material + rim type) plus what is visible in the reference photos. Not measured.
geometry_hints_3d.recommended_origin: Midpoint of the bridge on the front face of the frame

reference_images.note: All photos share the same camera angle: they differ in colour only, so they give no parallax. Treat this as a single-view reconstruction problem with several texture references.

items.camera_calibration: unknown — focal length, distance and sensor are not published

limitations: Multiple photos per model, but one per colourway and all from the same three-quarter angle — different finishes of the same geometry, not different viewpoints. There is no stereo baseline for photogrammetry.
Camera intrinsics are unknown and the view is perspective, so pixel distances cannot be converted to millimetres directly. Scale the finished model from `measurements_mm` instead.
The rear of the frame, the inner temple surfaces and the hinge interior are never visible.
The supplier gives a size range, not the size of the photographed unit.
`geometry_hints_3d` are construction defaults, not measurements of this frame.
